title: The Élysée Treaty was signed as a treaty of friendship between France and West Germany by President Charles de Gaulle and Chancellor Konrad Adenauer.
text: The Élysée Treaty was a treaty of friendship between France and West Germany, signed by President Charles de Gaulle and Chancellor Konrad Adenauer on 22 January 1963 at the Élysée Palace in Paris. With the signing of this treaty, Germany and France established a new foundation for relations, bringing an end to centuries of French–German enmity and wars.

title: West Berlin state election, 1963
text: The election to the West Berlin House of Representatives on 17 February 1963 was the first election in Berlin since the construction of the Berlin Wall. The top candidate of the SPD was again the mayor Willy Brandt while the CDU chose deputy mayor Franz Amrehn.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1963
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 1963 with the song "Marcel", written by Charly Niessen, and performed by Heidi Brühl. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Hessischer Rundfunk, selected its entry through a national final, after having previously selected the performer internally.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 1963

title: Rhineland-Palatinate state election, 1963
text: The 1963 Rhineland-Palatinate state election was conducted on 31 March 1963 to elect members to the Landtag, the state legislature of Rhineland-Palatinate, West Germany.

title: April 1 German broadcaster ZDF started.
text: ZDF, short for Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen (German: ; lit. 'Second German Television'), is a German public-service television broadcaster based in Mainz, Rhineland-Palatinate. Launched on 1 April 1963, it is run as an independent nonprofit institution, and was founded by all federal states of Germany (Bundesländer).

title: July 2 - 13th Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 13th annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from 21 June to 2 July 1963. The Golden Bear was jointly awarded to To Bed or Not to Bed directed by Gian Luigi Polidoro and Bushido, Samurai Saga directed by Tadashi Imai.

title: Ich bin ein Berliner is a quotation from a June 26, 1963, speech by U.S. President John F. Kennedy in West Berlin.
text: "Ich bin ein Berliner" is a speech by United States president John F. Kennedy given on June 26, 1963, in West Berlin. It is one of the best-known speeches of the Cold War and among the most famous anti-communist speeches.

title: The First Erhard cabinet led by Ludwig Erhard was sworn in.
text: The First Erhard cabinet was the government of West Germany between 17 October 1963 and 26 October 1965. Led by the Christian Democratic Union Ludwig Erhard, the cabinet was a coalition between the Christian Democratic Union and the Free Democratic Party (FDP).

title: East German general election, 1963
text: General elections were held in East Germany on 20 October 1963. They were to originally be held in November 1962 but were postponed.

title: Wunder von Lengede
text: On 7 November 1963, 11 West German miners were rescued from a collapsed mine after surviving for 14 days, an event that later became known as the Wunder von Lengede. title: Date unknown - Berliner Philharmonie is completed.
text: The Berliner Philharmonie is a concert hall in Berlin, Germany, and home to the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra. The Philharmonie lies on the south edge of the city's Tiergarten and just west of the former Berlin Wall.

title: “Junge, komm bald wieder” by Freddy Quinn
text: Freddy Quinn is a former Austrian singer and actor whose popularity in the German-speaking world soared in the late 1950s and 1960s. As Hans Albers had done two generations before him, Quinn adopted the persona of the rootless wanderer who goes to sea but longs for a home, family and friends.

title: “Schuld war nur der Bossa Nova” by Manuela
text: "Blame It on the Bossa Nova" is a song written by Cynthia Weil and Barry Mann that became a 1963 hit single for Eydie Gormé, reaching No. 7 on the Hot 100 in Billboard in March 1963.

title: “Barcarole in der Nacht” by Connie Francis
text: Concetta Rosa Maria Franconero, known professionally as Connie Francis, was an American singer and actress. One of the top-charting female vocalists of the late 1950s and early 1960s, she amassed over 200 million records sold, placing her among the best-selling music artists in history.

title: “Ich will 'nen Cowboy als Mann” by Gitte
text: Gitte Hænning is a Danish singer and film actress, who rose to fame as a child star in the 1950s. She was known primarily mononymously (without a surname) in Europe.

title: “Rote Lippen soll man küssen” by Cliff Richard
text: Lucky Lips is a song written by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller. It was originally recorded by Ruth Brown in 1956 and was successfully covered by Cliff Richard in 1963.
